text: Now Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the women of the land.
And Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of that region, saw her; he seized her, lay with her, and violated her.
And his soul clung to Dinah, Jacob's daughter; he loved the girl and spoke tenderly to her.

versions.text: But his heart was drawn to Dinah, Jacob's daughter; he loved the girl and spoke tenderly to her.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew דבק ("clung, was bound to") is stronger than "was drawn to," and the opening "But" imports a contrast not present in the Hebrew narrative sequence.

text: So Shechem said to his father Hamor, "Get me this girl as my wife."
Jacob heard that Shechem had defiled his daughter Dinah, but his sons were with his livestock in the field, so Jacob held his peace until they came home.
Then Hamor, Shechem's father, went out to Jacob to speak with him.

When Jacob's sons came in from the field and heard of it, the men were deeply grieved and burned with anger, because Shechem had done an outrageous thing in Israel by lying with Jacob's daughter—a thing that must never be done.
Hamor said to them, "My son Shechem has his heart set on your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife.
Intermarry with us: give us your daughters, and take our daughters for yourselves.
Settle among us. The land is open before you—live in it, trade in it, and acquire property in it."
And Shechem said to Dinah's father and brothers, "Let me find favor in your eyes, and I will give whatever you ask of me.
Set the bride-price and the gift as high as you like, and I will pay whatever you demand. Only give me the girl as my wife."
Jacob's sons answered Shechem and his father Hamor with deceit, because Shechem had defiled their sister Dinah.
They said to them, "We cannot do such a thing—give our sister to a man who is uncircumcised. That would be a disgrace to us.
We will consent to you on one condition only: that you become like us by having every male among you circumcised.
Then we will give you our daughters and take your daughters for ourselves. We will live among you and become one people.
But if you will not listen to us and be circumcised, we will take our daughter and go."
Their proposal seemed good to Hamor and to his son Shechem.
The young man lost no time in doing what they asked, because he was delighted with Jacob's daughter; and he was the most honored of all his father's household.
So Hamor and his son Shechem went to the gate of their city and spoke to the men of the city:
"These men are at peace with us. Let them settle in the land and trade in it; the land is large enough for them. We can take their daughters as our wives and give them our daughters.
But the men will consent to live with us and become one people on this one condition: that every male among us be circumcised, as they are circumcised.
Will not their herds, their property, and all their livestock become ours? Let us only give them our consent, and they will settle among us."
All the men who went out from the city gate listened to Hamor and his son Shechem, and every male was circumcised.
On the third day, while they were still in pain, two of Jacob's sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, took their swords, came against the unsuspecting city, and killed every male.
They put Hamor and his son Shechem to the sword, took Dinah out of Shechem's house, and left.
Jacob's sons came upon the slain and plundered the city, because its men had defiled their sister.

versions.text: Jacob's sons came upon the slain and plundered the city, because their sister had been defiled.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is active plural ("because they had defiled their sister"), implicating the townsmen; the passive rendering removes the agency that motivates the plunder of the whole city.

text: They seized the flocks, the herds, the donkeys, and everything else in the city and in the fields.
They took captive all their children and their wives, and carried off all their wealth and everything in the houses.

versions.text: They carried off all their wealth, their women, and their children, and plundered everything in the houses.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb שָׁבוּ specifically means "took captive," which the vague "carried off" obscures; the fate of the women and children is a distinct and important detail. The Hebrew also lists the little ones (טַף) before the wives.

text: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, "You have brought disaster on me by making me a stench to the inhabitants of this land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites. My men are few; if they band together against me and attack me, I and my household will be destroyed."
But they answered, "Should he treat our sister like a prostitute?"
